 COMMON JUDGMENT  These claim petitions are filed under Section 166 of M.V Act, 1988 seeking compensation for the injuries sustained in a road traffic accident.
As both petitions were arising out of the same accident, they were clubbed together for recording of common evidence and judgment.

2. The common facts leading to the filing of the top noted petitions are that on 24.11.2023 at about 8.40 a.m, when the petitioner in MVC-8352/2023 being accompanied by three pillion riders i.e., along with his wife and 2 children was riding a motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-06-EY-6994 near Urdigere Circle, Koratagere Town, Tumkur District, the driver of car bearing Reg.No.KA-01-H-5054 came at high speed in a rash &
negligent manner and dashed against their motorcycle.
Due to the tremendous impact they fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

After the accident both the petitioners were shifted to Government Hospital, Koratagere, wherein they took first aid and thereafter they were shifted to District Hospital, Tumkur wherein they took treatment as an outpatient and thereafter they took treatment as an inpatient at Aruna Hospital.

They are still under treatment and have spent considerable amount towards their medicines, conveyance and other incidental Nagaveni V R vs Malleshappa M B on 15 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/97229791/
2 expenses.

sentences.text: During the course of investigation material evidence connected to the accident was collected by them.
The Wound certificates marked at Ex's.P5 and 14 disclose that the petitioners sustained grievous injuries in a road traffic accident.
A close look at the spot mahazar indicates that accident has occurred in the manner as alleged by the petitioners.
Even the damages caused to both the vehicles as per IMV report supports this aspect.
Be that as it may, the IMV inspector has mentioned that he tested both the vehicles and found that their brake systems were in order.
He has thereby opined that the accident was not due to any mechanical defects of the said vehicles.
Therefore the driver of the car did not have sufficient cause to have lost control of his vehicle.

Such being the case, the very fact that he dashed against the motorcycle on which the petitioners were proceeding leads to drawing of an inference that he was driving his vehicle rashly & negligently.
Hence the jurisdictional police have also filed charge sheet against him for the offences punishable under section's 279, 337 & 338 of  9 SCCH-23  MVC.8352/2023 C/w MVC.8353/2023 IPC.
There is nothing on record to believe that the charge sheet filed by the police is defective or collusive.

sentences.text: Apart from that perusal of the written statement filed by the respondent No.2 shows that the insurance company has taken divergent stands.
At one stretch it has denied the very involvement of its insured vehicle and at another it has contended that there was no negligence on the part of driver of its insured vehicle.
Thus, absolutely there is no merit in the defence taken by respondent No.2.

The main contention of the insurance company is that the petitioner in MVC.8352/2023 (PW.1) who was riding his motorcycle with three persons on the pillion,
has contributed his negligence in the occurrence of the accident.
However the fact that PW.1 was riding a motorcycle accompanied by three pillion riders, may not, by itself, without anything more, make him guilty of contributory negligence.
At the most, he would be guilty of being a party to the violation of  10 SCCH-23  MVC.8352/2023 C/w MVC.8353/2023 law.

But such violation by itself, without anything more,
cannot lead to a finding of contributory negligence unless it is established that it is the very act of PW.1 riding along with there others contributed either to the accident or to the impact of the accident upon him and the other petitioners.
10. In this regard the respondnet No.2 relied the decision reported in 2003 0 Supreme (AP) 1460, in case of United India Insurance Company Limited v/s K. Anjaiah.

Therefore, in the absence of any evidence to show that the wrongful act on the part of PW.1 contributed either to the accident or to the nature of injuries sustained, he cannot be held guilty of contributory negligence.
Further to prove contributory negligence there must be cogent evidence.
In the case on hand there is no specific evidence to establish that the accident took place due to rash & negligent act of PW.1.
In the absence of same, the Doctrine of Common Law cannot be applied in the present case.
13. Interestingly the respondent No.2 which denied the very involvement of its insured car as well as the manner of occurrence of the accident has not led any evidence to this effect.
Further the insurance company did not make any attempt to examine the driver of its insured car who is the best witness to depose about the cause of accident.
There is no explanation to that effect.

Hence its contention  13 SCCH-23  MVC.8352/2023 C/w MVC.8353/2023 that there was no negligence on the part of driver of car has to be disbelieved.
Under such circumstances, the evidence of PW.1 & 2 which is supported by police documents has to be accepted.
